analysis: This PR is documentation-only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/sandbox-setup-work-disks.md) and updates to docs/provider/cli-reference.md describing `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>`. No source code is changed here, so no code-level regression can be shown from the supplied evidence. The behavior described touches TB-013/T-061 (CLI downloads and runs install.sh as the Mac owner) and A-019. The docs keep the existing posture: HTTPS-only download, redirects limited to https, 1 MiB cap, no CLI verification beyond TLS, installer verifies the add-on release. The new `--disk` passthrough passes absolute paths to the installer. Because stdin is closed and the installer is invoked with explicit argument vectors, I see no documented shell-injection path, but the Swift implementation (SandboxInstaller.swift, SandboxWorkDisk.swift) is not supplied, so argument quoting and path validation are unverified. The documented ownership-enable flow runs `sudo diskutil enableOwnership /Volumes/<name>` in the foreground process group after an explicit default-no prompt. The CLI never reads the password, and it never formats a drive. Residual question for code review: the volume name is attacker-influenced (a mounted volume can have an arbitrary name), so the displayed and executed command must be passed as an argv without shell interpretation. The docs also state a /Volumes/<name> must-be-the-mounted-volume check, which mitigates symlink or path spoofing, but this cannot be confirmed without code. The external drive holds VM images and jobs, not provider keys or the prefix cache (T-041 is unaffected; the cache storage is separate). I identified no threat-model gap needing an update from this docs change, though the implementation PR should confirm the sudo and argument handling.
